confidence_notes: I used two web searches. One gave the latest RBA rate. The other gave typical prices in Leh. Restaurant meal prices are fairly well supported: aggregated travel guides put budget meals at about Rs 150-250, mid-range meals at about Rs 250-500 per person, and a budget meal at about USD 3.50. A tripbase-style aggregated table gave coffee at about USD 2 and beer at about USD 2.50. However, the search did not find rupee prices for a cappuccino or a beer from current menus. Leh has few licensed bars, so I adjusted beer upward to about Rs 300-400 for a Kingfisher-type serving. Cocktail and wine prices are less certain. I estimated them from their usual relationship to beer prices and the limited, often imported wine on offer. July is peak tourist season in Leh, which raises prices. All accommodation figures are my own overall estimates for July. I did not check live booking pages or listings.
comparable_city_reasoning: Compared with Himalayan tourist towns in northern India such as Manali and McLeod Ganj. July is peak season, and Leh is remote, so supply costs are higher.
